editorial:
Imagine meeting a lonely boy who claims he has a secret friend that only he can see. That is exactly how you get pulled into this story. You will follow a struggling young man and a quiet boy who form a strange bond based on a lie. The vibe is very soft and sad, focusing on people who feel like they do not fit in anywhere. It is not a loud mystery with big clues, but rather a quiet look at how people use make-believe to deal with pain and loneliness in their real lives.

The acting is the best part here because the kids feel like real people, not movie characters. While the story moves slowly, the emotional payoff makes the wait worth it. If you enjoy stories that make you cry, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you really love the art style, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move to keep the beautiful visuals forever.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that the boy's secret friend was actually a girl who passed away. The boy created this fantasy to cope with his grief and loneliness. In the end, the adults and children learn to accept the truth about loss. The movie wraps up by showing that while lies can protect us for a while, being honest about our pain is the only way to actually heal and move forward.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories about friendship and healing.
